We simplify the expression step by step, naming the identity or technique used at each step.

Step 1. Factor out the common trigonometric factor.

\cos \theta \left(1 + \tan^2 \theta\right)

Step 2. Use the Pythagorean identity 1+\tan^2 \theta=\sec^2 \theta.

\cos \theta \sec^2 \theta

Step 3. Use the reciprocal identity to rewrite the secant or cosecant in terms of sine and cosine: \sec \theta=\frac{1}{\cos \theta} and \csc \theta=\frac{1}{\sin \theta}.

\cos \theta \cdot \frac{1}{\cos^2 \theta}

Step 4. Cancel the common factor in the numerator and denominator.

\frac{1}{\cos \theta}

Step 5. Use the reciprocal identity to write the result as a single trigonometric function.

Therefore the simplified expression is \boxed{\sec \theta}.
